_comment: A FILE, not a hard-coded list, for the same reason styles are files: these
are vocabulary, and vocabulary is the thing a user wants to change. Add,
reword or delete an entry here and it appears in the picker on restart.
Each entry: id (stable, referenced by saved prompts), label (shown), text
(the words appended to the prompt), hint (the tooltip), and for movements,
an svg key naming which preview diagram to draw.
TEXT IS THE PRODUCT. These phrasings are what actually reaches the model,
so they use the language image and video models were trained on -- the
vocabulary of a shot list, not of a camera manual. 'low angle, looking up'
outperforms 'camera elevation -20 degrees' by a wide margin on every
diffusion model here, because captions are written by people.
MOVEMENTS ARE VIDEO ONLY (video: true). A still cannot dolly, and asking a
text-to-image model for one wastes tokens on an instruction it can only

shot.label: Extreme close-up
shot.hint: Eyes, hands, a detail filling the frame

shot.label: Close-up
shot.hint: Head and shoulders; the face carries the frame

shot.label: Medium
shot.hint: Waist up; gesture and expression both read

shot.label: Cowboy
shot.hint: Mid-thigh up — stance reads, and so does the face

shot.label: Full
shot.text: full shot, head to toe in frame
shot.hint: The whole figure, with a little room

shot.label: Wide
shot.hint: Figure small against the place it is in

angle.label: Eye level
angle.hint: Neutral. The default a model assumes if you say nothing

angle.label: Low
angle.text: low angle, camera looking up at the subject
angle.hint: Makes the subject tower; power, threat, heroism

angle.label: High
angle.text: high angle, camera looking down at the subject

angle.label: Overhead
angle.text: overhead shot, straight down, bird's eye view
angle.hint: Straight down — pattern and geometry over character

angle.label: Ground
angle.text: extreme low angle from ground level
angle.hint: Lens on the floor, looking up

angle.label: Over shoulder
angle.hint: Past one person's shoulder onto another

lens.label: 14mm
lens.text: shot on a 14mm ultra-wide lens, strong perspective distortion

lens.label: 35mm
lens.hint: The documentary lens; close to how a room looks

lens.label: 50mm
lens.text: shot on a 50mm lens, natural perspective
lens.hint: Neutral. Roughly what the eye sees

lens.label: 85mm
lens.text: shot on an 85mm portrait lens, shallow depth of field

lens.label: 135mm
lens.text: shot on a 135mm telephoto lens, compressed background

lens.label: Macro
lens.text: macro lens, extreme detail, razor-thin depth of field
lens.hint: Texture at life size or closer

lens.label: Anamorphic
lens.text: anamorphic lens, wide cinematic frame, horizontal flares
lens.hint: Cinema scope look, oval bokeh, blue streaks

move.label: Static
move.hint: Tripod. Nothing moves but the subject

move.label: Push in
move.text: slow dolly push in toward the subject

move.label: Pull out
move.text: slow dolly pull back away from the subject

move.label: Pan left
move.hint: Pivots on the spot, to the left

move.label: Pan right
move.hint: Pivots on the spot, to the right

move.label: Orbit
move.hint: Circles the subject; shows it in the round

move.label: Tracking
move.text: tracking shot following alongside the subject
move.hint: Travels with the subject, keeping pace

move.label: Crane up
move.hint: Lifts away and up; the closing shot

move.label: Zoom in
move.hint: The LENS moves, not the camera — flatter than a push
